text:
maria: heads-up — i'm sketching UX/behaviour for per-tier canaries when smart routing + fallbacks are active. want to avoid surprising enterprises with silent fallbacks. thoughts?

devin: +1. main debate: attach rollout scope to the route config (per-route) or to the customer/tier mapping at runtime (per-tenant). route-level is simpler for devs, tenant-level gives more flexibility.

sam: telemetry concern — if a canary is 5% for enterprise but smart routing prefers cheaper variant in eu, our telemetry will split signals across variants/regions and make regression detection noisy. need canonical attribution.

anita: we should guarantee attribution keys: rollout_id, tier, region, chosen_variant. that makes dashboards joinable. also fallback_reason (e.g. quota, latency, model-unavailable).

tyler: console idea: exposure slider per tier + a checkbox "respect routing fallbacks" that shows projected exposure per-region/variant in a small table. avoids surprise.

maria: what about quota interplay? if enterprise has a higher quota cap and we fallback to a cheaper variant that's lower quality, customer might see different cost profile but still within quota. do we enforce a min-quality per-tier?

devin: configuration prototype i posted on the api loop, simplified:
```yaml
routes:
  /generate:
    rollout:
      id: r-2026-03-canary
      per_tier:
        enterprise:
          exposure: 0.05
          min_quality_score: 0.92
        standard:
          exposure: 0.02
      fallback_policy:
        - when: capacity_constraint
          allow_variants: [v1-quant, v1-int8]
          max_weight: 0.3
        - when: latency_spike
          allow_variants: [v1-fast]
```

devin: runtime would evaluate routing policy -> tier rules -> fallback policy. Fallback max_weight prevents full shift to cheaper variants unless explicit.

sam: alerting: gate on per-rollout per-tier p50/p95 latency and error_rate, but also on variant-heterogeneity metric (entropy of variant distribution). if entropy jumps, flag the rollout.

anita: agree. also add a "regression shadow" mode where we log outputs from both primary and fallback variants for a small subset to compare quality without impacting latency.

maria: UX questions: what does the developer see in the rollout timeline? show a stacked area of actual traffic broken down by variant+region+tier. include quick links to traces for slow requests.

tyler: implementable. small mock: shows stacked bars per-hour, hover reveals rollout id, variant, and % of tier traffic. also inline note if fallback_policy was invoked that hour.

rollout-bot: deployed canary r-2026-03-canary -> enterprise 5% in us-west; initial variant=v2; fallback allowed for capacity: [v1-quant] up to 30%

maria: action items: (1) devin to draft api schema for per_tier rollout + fallback max_weight (2) eng-runtime to add attribution headers (rollout_id, tier, region, chosen_variant, fallback_reason) (3) observability to add entropy/variant-split panels and per-rollout gates.

anita: can we also add a soft-fallback opt-out at tenant level? some customers require strict model pinning.

devin: yes — tenant config should be able to pin model families; runtime respects pinning before fallback rules.

sam: i'll prototype the entropy alert query and a quick dashboard row for rollout comparison.

maria: ok thanks team — let's sync tomorrow 10:30 to lock the schema. :thumbsup:
